# Avali
Avali are lightweight, feathered, raptor-like humanoids from a frigid world: pack hunters with wing-like arms, a long tail and big ears. Their ammonia-based biology makes them comfortable in the cold and miserable in the heat.
## Diet
- Eats fruit and meat, but not vegetables. - Theobromine (chocolate, tea, coffee) and allicin (onion, garlic) are poisonous to them.
## Benefits
- [color=#1e90ff]Cold-adapted[/color]: they take very little Cold damage and are slowed less by the cold than other species. - [color=#1e90ff]Zero-G specialists[/color]: pack-hunter instincts give Avali noticeably better acceleration when weightless.
## Special
- Their claws deal Slash damage. - Lighter than other species, with a lower natural body temperature. - Ammonia-based blood, and only half as much of it as most species, so standard blood transfusions won't help.
## Drawbacks
- [color=#ffa500]Heat-fragile[/color]: they start taking Heat damage at a lower temperature and take much more of it. Because of this, [color=red]Leporazine is highly dangerous[/color] and can be lethal at higher doses. - As a lightweight species they are frail, taking [color=#ffa500]30% more Blunt damage[/color] and [color=#ffa500]10% more Slash and Piercing damage[/color]. - For the same reason they lack muscle, [color=#ffa500]dealing 35% less Blunt damage[/color] and [color=#ffa500]15% less Slash damage[/color] in melee.
## Feathers
A heavy hit can tear out one of an Avali's feathers, which hurts and gives them a [color=#1e90ff]short burst of adrenaline[/color]. An Avali can lose up to three feathers, which slowly grow back. Feathers can also be [color=#1e90ff]preened[/color] out by hand from the context menu, either by the Avali or by someone else. A feather takes on its owner's colour, works as a quill, and can be worn behind an ear or in a hat.
## Voice
Avali speech comes through as chirps and trills with the Parrot speech verb. Besides the usual emotes, they can *chirp*, *trill*, *warble*, *purr* and *growl*, and have their own scream, laugh, cry and whistle.
